raw_response:
I've been working this same ground since I was a teenager. Fifty years gives you a feel for the land that no book can teach. My wife and I manage the farm mostly ourselves now — our son sends money from the city sometimes, but the fieldwork falls to me.

My main system is wheat and maize on the same 7 mu. I put wheat in around the first of October, right after the maize comes off. I've done this rotation so long I could do it in my sleep. The soil knows the rhythm. After the June wheat harvest I get the maize in fast — no time to waste in that window. The two crops together keep cash coming in twice a year from grain sales.

I keep 2 mu of cotton even though the young people say it doesn't pay anymore. I've grown cotton my whole life. I know exactly when the bollworm comes, I know how many waterings it needs, I can read the leaves. At my age I'm not going to switch to something new I don't understand. My back isn't what it was for picking, but 2 mu I can handle.

The stevia on the last 1.1 mu I started about five or six years ago. The buyers come through the village, they weigh it and pay cash. Better price per mu than grain. I grow enough to make it worth the trouble but not so much I can't manage the harvest.

For seeds I buy the township-recommended improved wheat variety every year — it holds up against rust better than the old stuff. For maize I always use hybrid. For cotton I use the BT hybrid; it costs more but I spray far less for bollworm than I used to. With the well I can irrigate when I need to, but I watch my pumping costs.

I won't change much this year. What I'm doing works.
